name: r-companion
description: Gets students to a working R setup in VS Code, then writes commented tidyverse code from menus: data and wrangling, a data viewer and coding sheet, reliability, descriptive statistics and charts, and the course's statistical tests.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In Restricted Mode the setup check runs R from a neutral folder and ignores folder settings that point at a program. Opening an R terminal and running the course setup script wait until you trust the folder.

commands.title: Run the course setup check script
Add the course's Copilot instructions to this folder
Import a data file (CSV or Excel)
Run my steps from the top
Show what is loaded in R (Workspace panel)

languageModelTools.name: aura_r_check_setup
languageModelTools.userDescription: Checks R and the packages the student's course needs. Changes no files and installs nothing.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Checks whether R and the packages the student's course needs (MC 451 or MC 501) are installed and working, and returns the checklist (OK, MISSING, or CHECK per item). Read-only: it installs nothing and changes no files. Use it when a student's R code fails because a package or R itself may be missing, or when they ask whether their setup works. To install what is missing, tell the student to run the command AURA: Install what is missing.

languageModelTools.name: aura_r_explain_error
languageModelTools.userDescription: Explains an R error message in plain English with the course's fix and help page. Changes no files.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Looks up an R error or warning message in the course's table of the messages students meet most often and returns a plain-English explanation, the fix steps the course teaches, and the course help page. Read-only. Pass the exact text R printed. If nothing matches, say so and explain the message yourself.

message.description: The error or warning text exactly as R printed it.

languageModelTools.name: aura_r_check_test_choice
languageModelTools.userDescription: Checks whether the statistical test a student chose fits their variables. It checks a choice; it does not choose.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Checks a statistical test the STUDENT has already chosen against the kind of variables they described, using the course's rules (chi-square for two categorical variables, Welch t-test for a numeric outcome across two groups, one-way ANOVA for three or more groups, linear regression or correlation for two numeric variables). Returns whether the choice fits and why. Choosing the test is graded work: never call this without the student's own choice, and never tell the student which test to use beyond what this tool returns.

outcome.description: The kind of variable the student is explaining or comparing (the outcome).

comparison.description: The kind of variable the outcome is compared across or predicted from.

enumDescriptions: Not set: the extension asks, or remembers your answer for this folder.
auraR.course.markdownDescription: Your course. Leave it empty and the extension asks once, then remembers your answer for the open folder.

auraR.rPath.markdownDescription: Full path to `Rscript` (or `Rscript.exe`). Leave it empty to let the extension find R: it checks this setting, then the R extension's `r.rpath` and `r.rterm` settings, then your PATH, then the Windows registry and the standard install folders.

auraR.cranMirror.markdownDescription: The CRAN mirror used by **Install what is missing**. Setting it means R never shows the long list of countries and cities.

auraR.runWith.markdownDescription: How the extension runs R code you can see. `auto` uses Positron inside Positron, the R extension (REditorSupport) when it is installed, and otherwise a plain R terminal with bracketed paste off.

enumDescriptions: On for MC 451 and MC 501, off for MC 427 (MC 427 does not let Copilot Agent mode run anything).
auraR.copilotTools.markdownDescription: The three tools GitHub Copilot Chat's agent mode can call: **Check my R setup**, **Explain an R error**, and **Check my test choice**. None of them changes a file or runs your analysis. `auto` turns them on for MC 451 and MC 501 and off for MC 427.

auraR.apaCheck.markdownDescription: Offer **APA numbers to check your sentence** in the Test menu: a short R block that prints a test's numbers in APA form from your own run, so you can check the numbers in the sentence you wrote. It never writes the sentence's words or a plain-English interpretation.

walkthroughs.title: AURA Lab R Companion: Get Started
walkthroughs.description: Four steps from a fresh install to a working R setup for MC 427, MC 451, or MC 501.

steps.title: Pick your course
steps.description:
Tell the extension which course you are in, so it checks the right packages.
[Pick my course](command:auraR.pickCourse)

steps.title: Check your setup
steps.description:
Find R, check each package your course needs, and install anything missing.
[Check my setup](command:auraR.checkSetup)

steps.title: Open your course workspace
steps.description:
Open the folder that holds your course files, so R can find them by name. Made your copy before this extension existed? Add the course's Copilot instructions to it.
[Open my course workspace](command:auraR.openCourseWorkspace)
[Add the Copilot instructions](command:auraR.addCourseFiles)

steps.title: Where to get help
steps.description:
Paste an R message to get a plain-English explanation, or open the help pages for your course.
[Explain an R error](command:auraR.explainError)
[Where to get help](command:auraR.getHelp)
